Payment reminder email for a cleaning business

Cleaning bills are small, repeat every week, and are easy to put off chasing. Here is a reminder schedule that fits, and wording to copy for homes and offices.

Checked 2026-11-21. Menus in other products change, so a label may differ slightly on your screen.

Short answer: send a friendly reminder on the due date, an overdue note three to five days later, a firmer one at about two weeks, and a final notice at about 30 days. Name the visit dates the invoice covers, attach the invoice, and give one way to pay. For a card that was declined, send a different message that asks them to update the card.

How a cleaning business bills, and why it changes the reminders

A plumber sends one invoice after one job. You do not. You clean the same house every other Tuesday, or the same office every night, and the money arrives in one of a few ways. Each way goes wrong differently.

  • Card on file. Nobody chases anything until a charge fails. A declined card is usually an expired card, not a refusal.
  • Invoice per visit or per month. The customer has to remember to pay, again and again. This is where the quiet late payers are.
  • Commercial accounts. The person who hired you is not the person who pays you. An accounts payable (AP) department pays, often on net 30 terms, and may reject an invoice with no purchase order (PO) number on it.

If you use QuickBooks Online, the built-in reminders are covered in how to automate invoice reminders in QuickBooks Online. They send the same words to everyone, which is a poor fit for a mix of homeowners and offices, and the standard reminders cannot leave one customer out. QuickBooks Online Advanced has workflows that can send reminders to chosen customers, but check how it works in your own company file. See how to stop QuickBooks invoice reminders for one customer.

A reminder schedule that suits cleaning

  1. On the due date, or 2 days before: a friendly heads-up. Homeowners on monthly billing often just forgot.
  2. 3 to 5 days late: a plain overdue note. Keep it short.
  3. About 14 days late: a firmer email that asks for a payment date. For a commercial client, send it to the AP contact as well as the person you deal with.
  4. About 30 days late: a final notice that says what happens next, such as pausing visits.

Cleaning invoices are small, so tighten the timing. If you clean weekly and wait a month to chase, four more visits have gone by. For more on spacing, see how often to send invoice reminders, and for the general method see how to chase overdue invoices by email.

Small amounts add up

A $90 balance feels too small to chase and too awkward to mention to a customer you like. Ten of them is $900. Write the reminder the same way whether it is $90 or $900. A short, polite email is not an accusation, and it keeps the habit from setting in.

When a card is declined

Do not use the overdue wording. Tell them the charge did not go through, say it is probably an expired or replaced card, and give a link or a number to update it. Send it the same day, then once more in three days. If your payment tool can retry the charge, tell the customer before it does. Check what your own payment tool allows.

Subject: Card declined for your cleaning on [date] Hi [name], The card we have on file for your cleaning service was declined on [date] for [amount]. This is usually an expired or replaced card. You can update it here: [pay link] If you would rather pay another way, just reply and tell me. Thanks. [your name]

Wording you can copy

1. Friendly, on or before the due date

Subject: Invoice [invoice number] for your cleaning, due [due date] Hi [name], A quick reminder that invoice [invoice number] for [amount] is due on [due date]. It covers the visits on [visit dates]. A copy is attached. You can pay here: [pay link] If it is already paid, thank you, and please ignore this. [your name]

2. Overdue, a few days late

Subject: Invoice [invoice number] is past due Hi [name], Invoice [invoice number] for [amount] was due on [due date] and I do not see a payment yet. It covers the visits on [visit dates]. A copy is attached. You can pay here: [pay link] If something on the invoice looks wrong, such as a visit we missed, tell me and I will fix it. [your name]

3. Firmer, about two weeks late

Subject: Invoice [invoice number] is now [days] days overdue Hi [name], Invoice [invoice number] for [amount] was due on [due date] and is still unpaid. A copy is attached. Could you let me know by [date] when we can expect payment? If there is a problem with the invoice or the visits it covers, call me on [phone] and we will sort it out. You can pay here: [pay link] [your name]

4. Final notice, about 30 days late

Subject: Final notice: invoice [invoice number] Hi [name], Invoice [invoice number] for [amount] is now [days] days overdue and I have not heard back about my earlier reminders. Please pay by [date]. If I do not hear from you by then, we will [pause your cleaning visits / add the late fee in our service agreement]. If something has gone wrong on your side, call me on [phone] and we can agree a plan. [your name]

5. A short text message

Only text a customer who agreed to receive texts from you, for example when they gave you their number and said texting was fine. Rules on consent differ, so check yours. Keep the text to one line and offer to stop.

Hi [name], this is [your name] from [business]. Invoice [invoice number] for [amount] is past due. You can pay here: [pay link]. Reply STOP to stop texts.

Disputes over skipped and extra visits

Many late payments are really disagreements. The customer says you skipped the 12th. You say they cancelled too late. Or a deep clean was added and nobody wrote it down.

  • List the visit dates and what each charge covers on the invoice itself. A line that says "March cleaning" starts arguments. A line that says "visits on March 3, 10, 17, 24" does not.
  • Write down cancellation and skip rules in the service agreement, and quote them in a reminder only if the customer is arguing a charge they agreed to.
  • If a visit was missed on your side, credit it before you send a reminder. Chasing a charge you know is wrong costs you the customer.
  • If they have raised a problem, stop the standard reminders and answer the problem first.

Commercial clients and purchase orders

Before the first invoice, ask who in AP receives invoices, which email they use, whether they need a PO number, and how long they take to pay. Many AP departments reject an invoice that has no PO number on it. Put the PO number on the invoice itself. When you chase, write to AP, copy your contact, and ask a question AP can answer: "Has this been approved for payment, and what is the expected pay date?"

Money and legal care

Late fees and their amounts depend on your agreement with the customer and on state law. Only state a consequence you are willing to carry out. This is not legal advice.
